scope: Actual native COPY-barrier backend interruption: non-atomic partial-state control, single-transaction schema/data rollback and clean retry; full app/private-media restore uses the same probes before atomic pg_restore.

localVerification.localFullComposeBlock: Current normal proxy probe of storage.googleapis.com returns CONNECT 403; MinIO Go dependencies use this redirect host. Full current-source Compose acceptance is required in ordinary independent GitHub Actions.

observedFailure: An interrupted --exit-on-error restore left two visible fixture tables. Stop-on-error does not make a whole restore atomic.
fix: Final native restore now uses pg_restore --exit-on-error --single-transaction into an isolated empty target. Two interruption controls demonstrate the before/after behavior; target identity and volume ownership are checked before reset.
safety: Generated restore projects only. The new guard rejects source/real/malformed targets before any SQL callback. Local fixture uses tmpfs, --network none, no host ports/real env; full Compose resets only its separately labelled restore DB.
ciAcceptance: Require both core and Compose jobs on the exact new source. Complete report must retain all prior auth/media/tenant/SMTP checks, two real interruption cases, atomic rollback, successful atomic retry and matching private-media restore after original source volumes were removed.
limits: Backend termination during a deterministic synthetic COPY pause is verified; client/network loss, server/container crash and other interruption points are distinct cases.

Single-transaction fixture restore does not establish backup completeness, PITR/WAL replay, encrypted-provider credential recovery, interrupted migration/upgrade behavior, in-flight queue restoration or production sizing/retention.
Live-provider/deployed and full master acceptance remain open; CI verifies and does not deploy.
